state.task: Settle ambiguous design choices of the real-time emergency director of CHOOGuard (FPS emergency-response training game, KORAIL station staff at a digital twin of Busan Station). Typed judgments only; JEV answers are advisory (authority 0); the main model implements and the user's words win.
user_decisions_already_made: JEV makes emergencies by judgement in real time, from objects and people that exist in the map
the director is event-driven (re-judge the moment a new candidate appears or disappears, a hazard changes, or a train/door/escalator situation starts) plus a one-second heartbeat

JEV rates each candidate's imminence on verbal levels, all candidates batched as independent questions in one request over a focused state; code owns the table from level to hazard rate and draws with competing risks over elapsed game time

first 30 seconds of a shift are quiet; the first emergency then comes after about three minutes on average; new separate emergencies are rare; about one to two new emergencies per fifteen to twenty minute shift
all JEV use together costs at most 3 US dollars per hour of play

facts.candidates_per_listing: about 30 in a calm shift and 40 to 60 during an incident; each rating question costs roughly 220 input tokens
facts.jev_1_13_weaknesses: numbers, counting, dates and time windows; reads conditions literally; large irrelevant state hurts
facts.measured_ratings: in a calm shift JEV puts most candidates on the level 'possible but unremarkable' and a few on 'somewhat favoured'; during a big fire it rates unrelated candidates higher than in calm even when told the fire is no reason
facts.listing_cost: listing all candidates takes a few milliseconds on the game's main thread
facts.candidate_lists_change: only when the world changes, because people and objects are picked by a stable per-shift rank

rate_from_score.instructions: A candidate's imminence was rated as a probability per verbal level. Which way of turning that into the candidate's hazard rate is right?

criteria.expected_rate_over_levels: The hazard is the sum over levels of the probability of the level times the game's rate for that level, so unlikely high levels still count in proportion
criteria.draw_one_level_then_rate: Draw one level from the probabilities every time and use that level's rate, so the hazard jumps between draws
criteria.most_probable_level_rate: Use the rate of the single most probable level and ignore the rest

rating_reuse.instructions: How long should a candidate's rating be reused before JEV is asked about it again?

criteria.until_changed_or_stale: Until the candidate's description changes, the situation in the state changes (a hazard, the train stage, staff response, agencies) or the rating is about a dozen seconds old
criteria.ask_all_every_heartbeat: Ask about every candidate on every one-second heartbeat
criteria.ask_only_on_events: Ask only when something happens and never on a timer

origin_frequency_scaling.instructions: The game will gain much more equipment, so many more candidate causes will be listed. The user wants the same overall frequency of new emergencies. What should the game do?

criteria.share_one_budget_above_reference: Keep every candidate's rate as calibrated while at most the calibrated number of origins is listed, and scale all origin rates down in proportion when more are listed
criteria.per_candidate_rate_only: Give every candidate its own rate from its rating and let the overall frequency rise as candidates are added
criteria.normalise_always_to_total: Always rescale so the sum of all rates equals a fixed total, whatever the ratings are

lost_judging_time.instructions: JEV was silent or over budget for a while and then answers again. What should happen to the game time in between?

criteria.no_catch_up: Time nobody judged is not made up: the draw covers at most a few seconds since the last step, and ratings older than half a minute stop counting
criteria.catch_up: Draw over the whole silent stretch with the latest ratings so no hazard is lost
criteria.pause_the_game: Stop the game clock until JEV answers

apply_validation.instructions: A draw picked a candidate, and JEV then needs another moment to rate how strongly it plays out. How should the game confirm the candidate still applies when the strength arrives?

criteria.list_again_and_require_same_key: List the candidates again and apply only if the same key naming that person, thing or place is still a candidate; otherwise nothing happens
criteria.require_identical_description: Apply only if the candidate's whole description text is identical to what JEV rated

candidate_identity.instructions: How should the people and places that become candidates be picked from a larger pool each time the list is rebuilt?

criteria.stable_rank_per_subject: Each subject gets one random rank per shift when first met, from a random stream of its own; lists pick by rank so they change only when the world does
criteria.reroll_each_listing: Pick randomly again at every listing

separate_emergency_framing.instructions: While an emergency is being handled, how should JEV be asked about a separate new emergency?

criteria.same_question_with_load_in_state_and_anc: Same imminence question as in calm, the load in the state, and level texts that say the emergency in progress is not a reason for it
criteria.no_question_only_code_rate: Do not ask JEV; give every separate cause a fixed tiny rate in code
criteria.ask_with_calm_state_only: Ask JEV with a state that hides the emergency in progress
